issues.detail: The tuple of error message types contains 'transcriber_error' twice. Either the author copy-pasted carelessly and meant a different string, or this is just dead noise. Either way, it's wrong. A maintainer reading this six months from now will waste time wondering whether one of them was supposed to be something else. Remove the duplicate, or fix the typo if one was intended.

issues.description: push_error called with str where ErrorFrame expected (per PR description)
issues.detail: The PR description says 'Add error frame for all error types' but push_error is being passed a keyword arg error_msg=f'...'. If push_error's signature wants an ErrorFrame, this is wrong; if it accepts a string and wraps it, fine, but the diff doesn't show enough context to tell. The pre-existing code did the same thing, so this isn't a regression — but it's worth verifying the contract instead of assuming. Show me the push_error signature.

issues.description: Error logging dropped in the consolidation
issues.detail: The old code logged each error category with logger.error before push_error. The new consolidated branch only calls push_error and skips the logger.error entirely. That's a behavior change that isn't mentioned in the changelog. push_error may or may not log — and if it does, fine, but the diff silently removes three logger.error calls. Either restore a single logger.error(f'ElevenLabs {message_type}: {error_msg}') before the push, or state explicitly that push_error handles logging.

issues.description: Commit/PR is two patches stuffed into one
issues.detail: This is THREE-PATCHES territory, or at least TWO-PATCHES. Patch 1: remove the swallowing try/except wrapper so the outer reconnect loop sees the disconnect. Patch 2: expand the error message_type list. They're unrelated changes touching different concerns. Squashing them makes bisect worse and review harder. Not a blocker on a small PR like this, but worth noting.
The diff shows '\ No newline at end of file' on changelog/3233.fixed.md. Trivial nit but it's the kind of thing a maintainer's linter will scream about. Add the newline.

issues.description: Default error string for unknown_error fallback is ugly
issues.detail: data.get('error', f'Unknown error - {message_type}') — the format 'Unknown error - quota_exceeded_error' reads worse than the prior per-branch defaults like 'Quota exceeded'. Minor regression in human-readable error text. Acceptable tradeoff for the consolidation, but worth noting.

review.summary: The core fix is right and the diagnosis is correct — the inner try/except was swallowing the disconnect and starving the outer reconnect loop. Deleting it is GOOD-TASTE: the special case existed to do nothing useful and removing it makes the control flow obvious. The error-type consolidation is fine in shape but sloppy in execution: duplicate 'transcriber_error' entry, three logger.error calls silently dropped, and a missing trailing newline in the changelog. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK. Fix the duplicate, restore or justify the dropped logging, add the newline, and this lands.
